_provenance.what: Real responses from the live Oxynet API, used for every number in Part Two of the manual.
_provenance.source_file: public/test_data.json, de-identified (id, file, path and user fields removed)
_provenance.how_to_refresh: See manual/README.md. Upload data/reference-test.json through create_upload, then analyze_cpet and compute_metrics, and paste the responses back here. Do not hand-edit the numbers.
_provenance.note: The thresholds stored in the source export (LT 1540, RCP 1940 mL/min) were set by the clinician who ran the test and were not shown to the model.

load.reason: the exercise_threshold_app export carries no work-rate or speed column, so this test has no external load. Nothing is inferred from VO2: back-calculating watts from oxygen uptake assumes the efficiency that a load channel would be used to measure

eov.headline: OSCILLATION PRESENT: TOO FAST FOR EOV, NOT GRADED
eov.summary: Breathing cycled every 21 seconds for 0.7 minutes, swinging 17% of ventilation, 7× above background, with CO₂ moving opposite. Faster than the 40–140 s the EOV definitions cover, so not graded as EOV, but not a normal pattern either.
eov.gas_quality_note: Gas analysis confirmed: CO₂ output followed ventilation to within 14°, and end-tidal CO₂ and O₂ held opposite to within 2°, and the end-tidal CO₂ waveform kept its shape (distortion 0.71, against a limit of 3.0), all as the physiology requires, so the traces behind this assessment are sound.
notes: No external load was recorded, so the protocol is unknown and nothing here is read against a work rate.

crossover.reason: Carbohydrate was already the larger fuel at the lowest intensity measured, so the crossover happened below anything this test covered.

efficiency.reason: Gross efficiency is mechanical work over metabolic energy, so it needs a work rate in watts. This test recorded no external load.

flags.detail: Rest and recovery are excluded: 37 resting samples were dropped before the windows were taken. Warm-up is kept: it is a real intensity and often the one FATMAX lands on.

This recording carries no external load, so substrate use is placed against %VO2peak only. FATMAX is reported as an intensity and cannot be given as a work rate, and gross efficiency needs mechanical power, so it is not computed.

6 of 12 windows sit above RER 1.0, where exhaled CO2 includes a non-metabolic part from buffering the metabolic acidosis. The stoichiometry does not hold there, so the fat rate at those intensities is an upper bound that reads low and can read negative, not a measurement.

method: Fat (g/min) = 1.695 × VO2 − 1.701 × VCO2, carbohydrate (g/min) = 4.585 × VCO2 − 3.226 × VO2, both with the gases in L/min (Frayn 1983; Jeukendrup and Wallis 2001), assuming protein oxidation is negligible.
Energy from each: 9.75 kcal per gram of fat and 4.18 kcal per gram of carbohydrate.

FATMAX is the peak of a cubic through the origin fitted to the fat rate against the axis shown (Achten and Jeukendrup). It is a fitted turning point, not a measured sample, and it carries no confidence.

gas_quality.note: Gas channels agree with each other as the physiology requires.

clock_integrity.note: Clock is monotonic; no repair needed.

landmarks.reading: Corroboration only. These are classical criteria computed on the file's own signal; they are not calibrated against outcomes, they carry no confidence, and they never override a model's thresholds. A V-slope with S1 below 1 and S2 above it is the expected shape; slopes that barely differ mean no breakpoint was found.

capabilities.retention: Uploaded bytes are parsed and discarded, never stored. The parsed record is deleted after 24 h.
